subject: Re: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite

Hi all —

We need to land the rollout plan for perf gates on the runtime release train now that Run 1 baselines are close to locked.

Goal: make baseline drift actionable without turning CI into a roulette wheel (variance/fleet noise) or paging SRE for non-issues.

Proposal (please poke holes):

PHASE 0 (current):
- PR-level "perf smoke" job runs on key microbenches; non-blocking (warn-only)
- Summary comment on PR + artifact upload for perf-canary ingestion

PHASE 1 (target: Feb 24 release train):
- Release-candidate builds (RC) require baseline suite run in perf-canary (nightly/adhoc)
- If baseline delta exceeds thresholds, release is blocked unless exception approved

PHASE 2 (target: Mar 10 release train):
- Make PR gate blocking for changes that touch scheduler/kernels/telemetry timing paths (path-based + label-based)
- Everything else remains warn-only until we have stable signal

Threshold sketch (aligned to variance budget work):
- TTFT p95 regression > +5% OR +15ms (whichever is larger)
- TPOT p95 regression > +5%
- E2E p99 regression > +8% (tail guardrail)
- Throughput regression > -5%
- Any error-rate increase > +0.2pp absolute

Exception workflow language (draft):
- Exception requires: (1) scoped rollback plan, (2) perf impact explained (kernel vs scheduler vs fleet vs telemetry), (3) sign-off from Release Eng + Runtime owner + SRE on-call delegate
- Exceptions expire in 14 days (must be re-justified or reverted)

Questions I need answered this week:
1) Sahana: can CI support the Phase 2 path/label gating without a bunch of false triggers?
2) Sean: what’s the right operational stance for failures (page vs ticket vs Slack-only)?
3) Mateo: are the dates realistic for Runtime to absorb?

Related: ENG-4828 (CI policy), ENG-4833 (release qualification checklist update).

Thanks,
Connor
Release Engineering | Redwood Inference


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite

This is directionally right.

Two asks:
- We need an explicit “what counts as the baseline environment” clause (driver/CUDA/runtime build stamp) or we will spend half of March arguing about drift.
- Phase 2: I’m okay with blocking for scheduler/kernels, but we should have an escape hatch for emergency fixes (security, correctness) without a full baseline suite rerun.

On dates: Feb 24 for RC gating is fine if it’s limited to RC builds and not every PR. Mar 10 for PR blocking might be aggressive unless the variance budgets are actually tight.

Mateo


From: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 11:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite

On Phase 2 mechanics:

- Path-based gating is doable (we already do this for some security scans), but it gets messy with generated code + shared libs. I can implement a conservative matcher:
  - /runtime/scheduler/**
  - /runtime/kernels/**
  - /runtime/telemetry/** (timing-only?)
  - plus "perf-gate" label to force-run

- Strong preference: don’t rely on “touching telemetry” as a trigger unless we’re specific. Otherwise any metrics refactor will block merges.

- Biggest issue is runtime of the job. The PR smoke job is OK (~20–25 min). The full baseline suite is not.

So for Phase 2 I’m interpreting “blocking PR gate” == blocking on perf smoke only, with baseline suite continuing to run in perf-canary nightly + on RC.

If that matches what you meant, I can get this into the release train config by the end of next week.

Sahana
CI / Release Automation


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 12:07 PM PT
Subject: Re: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite

+1 to keeping the full baseline suite out of PR CI.

Operational stance (for perf-canary nightly + RC gating):
- Nightly baseline failures should NOT page by default.
- Page only when (a) we’re in an RC window AND (b) delta crosses “severe regression” threshold AND (c) it reproduces on rerun OR is clearly environment-pinned.

I’d recommend we define two levels:

WARN:
- exceeds regression threshold but within 2x variance budget OR only on 1 region
- action: Slack notification to #eng-runtime + create ticket tagged “perf-regression”

SEVERE:
- exceeds threshold and reproduces, or multiple regions/hardware
- action: Slack + page (during RC window only)

Also: please explicitly call out that a “fleet mismatch / driver drift” is not a runtime regression, and the first action is to validate env stamps.

Sean
SRE


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 2:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite

This is helpful — thanks.

Clarifying intent: yes, Phase 2 “blocking” is perf smoke only, not full suite.

Mateo: agreed on “baseline environment” clause + emergency escape hatch.

Here’s revised policy language (please review):

---
Perf Gate Rollout (Q1 2026)

A) Gate types
1. PR Perf Smoke (CI)
- Scope: key microbenchmarks + minimal representative shapes
- Duration target: <30 minutes
- Output: structured artifact (includes git SHA, runtime build stamp, driver/CUDA versions)

2. Baseline Suite (perf-canary)
- Scope: full representative workload suite (streaming/non-streaming, long-context, bursty concurrency, cache scenarios)
- Run modes: nightly scheduled + ad-hoc RC qualification

B) Rollout phases
Phase 0 (now):
- PR Perf Smoke runs warn-only and posts PR summary

Phase 1 (Feb 24 release train):
- RC builds require Baseline Suite pass
- Blocking rule: release cannot be promoted if any SEVERE regression is present

Phase 2 (Mar 10 release train):
- PR Perf Smoke becomes blocking ONLY for runtime scheduler + kernels + explicitly enumerated perf-critical paths
- Non-perf-critical PRs remain warn-only

C) Regression thresholds (draft)
- TTFT p95: > +5% or +15ms (larger)
- TPOT p95: > +5%
- E2E p99: > +8%
- Throughput: < -5%
- Error rate: > +0.2pp absolute

D) Severity classification
WARN:
- regression beyond threshold but within variance budget allowances OR isolated to a single region/SKU

SEVERE:
- regression beyond threshold that reproduces on rerun OR occurs across multiple regions/SKUs

E) Exception process
- Exceptions permitted for:
  1) correctness/security fixes
  2) known + accepted perf tradeoffs with mitigation/rollback
- Required fields:
  - root-cause hypothesis (kernel/scheduler/telemetry/fleet)
  - rollback plan
  - owner + ETA for follow-up
- Sign-off required: Release Eng (Connor) + Runtime owner (Mateo delegate acceptable) + SRE delegate (Sean delegate acceptable)
- Expiration: 14 days

F) Baseline environment requirement
- Any gating decision must reference artifacts produced with:
  - pinned driver/CUDA versions
  - runtime build metadata stamp
  - hardware SKU + region recorded
- If env stamp does not match the baseline environment matrix, result is “invalid” (rerun required; not a regression).
---

Sahana: if you can implement the path matcher + “perf-gate” override label, that should cover us.

Sean: the WARN/SEVERE split is exactly what we need; I’ll mirror that in the release checklist update.

If no objections, I’ll treat this as the language to paste into the release train playbook and link from ENG-4833.

Connor


From: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite

Looks good.

Action items on my side:
- Add conservative path matcher (scheduler/kernels + allowlist for perf-critical files)
- Add “perf-gate” label to force-run (and “perf-gate-skip” only for emergency? I’d prefer not to add skip unless Mateo insists)
- Ensure CI artifact includes env stamp fields (driver, CUDA, SKU, region, runtime build stamp)

I can get a PR up by Friday.

Sahana


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 10:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite

No objections.

One tweak: make it explicit that “reproduces on rerun” means rerun on the same pinned environment (same driver/CUDA + same SKU pool). Otherwise we’ll chase ghosts.

For paging: I’m fine if you write “page only during RC window” — outside RC, ticket + Slack.

Sean


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 4:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: Release train: perf gates rollout (warn-only → blocking) for Q1 baseline suite

Perfect — incorporated Sean’s rerun clarification + the RC-only paging rule.

Mateo: on the emergency escape hatch, I’m going to phrase it as “exceptions allowed for correctness/security” (no special CI skip label). That keeps the process explicit and auditable.

Next steps:
- I’ll update the release qualification checklist (ENG-4833) with Phase 1 requirements.
- Sahana to land the path/label gate work in CI.
- I’ll send a short internal announcement once we have the CI change merged so teams aren’t surprised when Phase 1 starts on Feb 24.

Connor
